positive.prompt: Generate release notes for this pull request: https://github.com/acme/app/pull/42
Write release notes for release/2.4.0 from the issues it closes
Summarize this release PR for a non-technical audience

negative.prompt: Write a formal change record with rollback steps for this database change
Create a testing checklist for this story

evals.prompt: Generate release notes for release PR 42 (head branch release/2.4.0). Its body says: Closes #11, Closes #7. Issue 11 is labeled BE and titled '[BE] Upgrade Spring Boot to 4.1.2'. Issue 7 is labeled bug, FE and titled 'Device list shows duplicates after search'. Today is Oct 29, 2026. Address the summary to @jane.doe.
evals.expected_output: One raw markdown block with a versioned heading, two bullets in PR-body order with correct prefixes and links, and a two-sentence closing summary.
expectations: The response contains one fenced markdown block starting with '## Release Notes 2.4.0 (Oct 29, 2026)'
Bullets appear in the order #11 then #7, each with a [#n](https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/issues/<n>) hyperlink
The #11 bullet uses 'BE:' and ends its sentence with 'No user impact' and avoids version numbers and framework jargon
The #7 bullet uses 'BugFix FE:' and describes the outcome in one plain-English sentence
The block ends with a blank line and a two-sentence summary addressed to the recipient given in the prompt that ends with 'If you notice any issues in these areas, please let us know.'

evals.prompt: Generate release notes for release PR 50 (release/3.0.1). Its body says: Fixes #5. Issue 5 is titled 'Refactor sync job' with no labels and a body that only says 'see design doc'.
evals.expected_output: A single bullet with a best-reading description and a 'Please confirm' list after the code block.
expectations: The notes contain exactly one bullet for #5 with one sentence and a hyperlink
The behavior is not invented beyond what the ticket states
A 'Please confirm' list appears after the code block naming #5 and its missing label or details
